description: Issue #862: EtlDeadLetterRow now implements ITenant (its TenantCode column was already populated by the pipeline but never used for filtering). This mutant deletes the ApplyEtlTenantFilter<EtlDeadLetterRow>(builder, context) call in ApplyEtlModels(ModelBuilder, EmptyContext), reproducing the exact pre-fix behaviour: a context scoped to tenant A can read tenant B's EtlDeadLetterRow (including RowJson, the actual quarantined source data) by id. Checked against EtlTenantIsolationTests.EtlDeadLetterRow_TenantA_CannotReadTenantB_Row, which seeds two EtlDeadLetterRow rows under two different tenants and asserts a context scoped to tenant A cannot resolve tenant B's row -- with the mutant applied, that read succeeds and the assertion fails. The green control, EtlDeadLetterRow_TenantA_CanReadOwnRow, asserts tenant A can still read its OWN row, proving the mutation has no broader collateral effect (e.g. breaking the EtlDeadLetterRows table registration itself).

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.EtlTenantIsolat: #862: a context scoped to tenant A must NOT resolve tenant B's EtlDeadLetterRow by GUID

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against the committed baseline (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first; mutant patch applied via git apply, test run, then reverted via git apply -R): 'Assert.IsNull failed. #862: a context scoped to tenant A must NOT resolve tenant B's EtlDeadLetterRow by GUID -- RowJson holds the actual source rows that failed, so this is a real cross-tenant data-content read if it succeeds.' Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant etl862-applyetlmodels-deadletterrow-tenantfilter-neutralize: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
